dedupe_keys.name: grail gas reliability analysis integrated library

description: GRAIL is a prototype tool for intra-day model-predictive control of midstream natural gas pipeline systems, with algorithms for pipeline optimisation, optimal control and simulation. It was released in 2018 by Los Alamos National Laboratory with Anatoly Zlotnik as developer, building on published work on optimal control of transient gas flow. The model resolves dynamic flows through long pipes with a non-ideal gas equation of state on a simplified network, and provides optimal intra-day flow schedules and spatiotemporal economic values of gas while respecting hydraulic limits, compressor station constraints, operating factors and existing shipping contracts. Inputs are a pipeline model and time series of boundary conditions and constraints, placed in a model folder; outputs are time series of an approximately optimal solution. It runs in MATLAB with the IPOPT solver or can be compiled to an executable for the MATLAB runtime. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub under the BSD 3-Clause licence at no cost. Caveats: it is a prototype on simplified networks, the last commit was in October 2019, and it needs MATLAB or its runtime. Simulation uses are gas pipeline operation under changing demand. Related records: model-lanl-phydras-hydrogen-blending-pipelines extends this work to hydrogen blending.
